content: Let $f(t) \stackrel{FS}{\longleftrightarrow} a_n$, $g(t) \stackrel{FS}{\longleftrightarrow} b_n$. Both T-periodic, and let both f and g be in $L_{\mathbb{C}}^2[0, T]$.
Consider the inner product defined as:
\langle f, g \rangle = \frac{1}{T} \int_0^T f(t) g^\ast(t) dt \text{ on } L_{\mathbb{C}}^2[0, T]
\Rightarrow \langle f, g \rangle = \frac{1}{T} \int_0^T \left[ \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a_n e^{j \frac{2\pi}{T} n t} \right] \left[ \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} b_m e^{\frac{j 2\pi}{T} m t^\ast} \right] dt
